\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier degree of an affine sign linear form]
\lean{FABL.fourierDegree_affineSignLinearForm_le_one}
\label{FABL.fourierDegree_affineSignLinearForm_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.expect_monomial_mul, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierDegree, FABL.fourierDegree_le_iff, FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $a_0\in\mathbb R$, and let
$a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb R$. The function $x\mapsto a_0+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$ on
$\{\pm1\}^n$ has Fourier degree at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive threshold sign implies a nonnegative input]
\lean{FABL.thresholdSign_eq_one_nonneg}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p113-b003}
\label{FABL.thresholdSign_eq_one_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.thresholdSign, FABL.thresholdSign_of_neg}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $t$, if its threshold sign is $1$, then $0\le t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Negative threshold sign implies a negative input]
\lean{FABL.thresholdSign_eq_neg_one_neg}
\label{FABL.thresholdSign_eq_neg_one_neg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.thresholdSign, FABL.thresholdSign_of_nonneg}
\difficulty{3}
For every real number $t$, if its threshold sign is $-1$, then $t<0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive shift for threshold signs]
\lean{FABL.exists_positive_strict_shift}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p114-b001}
\label{FABL.exists_positive_strict_shift}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_neg_one, FABL.signValue_one, FABL.thresholdSign, FABL.thresholdSign_eq_neg_one_neg, FABL.thresholdSign_eq_one_nonneg}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\alpha$ be a finite set, let $f:\alpha\to\{ -1,1\}$, and let $p:\alpha\to\mathbb R$
satisfy $f(x)=1$ when $p(x)\geq 0$ and $f(x)=-1$ when $p(x)<0$. There is a real number
$c>0$ such that $f(x)(p(x)+c)>0$ for every $x\in\alpha$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integer coefficients for a strict representation]
\lean{FABL.exists_integer_coefficients_of_strict_representation}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p134-b003}
\label{FABL.exists_integer_coefficients_of_strict_representation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\iota$ be a finite index type and $\alpha$ a finite set, and let $f$ assign a sign
to each element of $\alpha$. Given real-valued features on $\iota\times\alpha$ and real
coefficients that represent $f$ strictly—meaning the sign of $f(x)$ times the resulting
feature sum is positive for every $x$—there are integer coefficients that still
represent $f$ strictly.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict sign representation]
\lean{FABL.representation_and_ne_zero_of_strict}
\label{FABL.representation_and_ne_zero_of_strict}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_neg_one, FABL.thresholdSign, FABL.thresholdSign_of_neg, FABL.thresholdSign_of_nonneg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ be a type, let $f$ assign to each $x\in X$ a sign in $\{-1,1\}$, and let
$p:X\to\mathbb{R}$. Suppose that for every $x\in X$, the value of the sign $f(x)$
multiplied by $p(x)$ is strictly positive. Then for every $x\in X$, $f(x)=1$ when
$p(x)\geq 0$ and $f(x)=-1$ when $p(x)<0$, and $p(x)\neq 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier expansion of a low-degree function]
\lean{FABL.sum_lowDegree_fourierCoeff_eq}
\label{FABL.sum_lowDegree_fourierCoeff_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierDegree, FABL.fourierDegree_le_iff, FABL.fourier_expansion, FABL.lowDegreeFourierFamily, FABL.monomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,d$ be nonnegative integers and let $p:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fourier degree
at most $d$. For every $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, $p(x)$ equals the sum over all subsets
$S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le d$ of the Fourier coefficient of $p$ at $S$ multiplied by
the monomial indexed by $S$ evaluated at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial expansion over low-degree subsets]
\lean{FABL.multilinearPolynomial_eq_sum_lowDegree}
\label{FABL.multilinearPolynomial_eq_sum_lowDegree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.lowDegreeFourierFamily, FABL.monomial, FABL.multilinearPolynomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,d$ be natural numbers, let $z$ assign an integer to each subset of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ of size at most $d$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. Form a multilinear
polynomial whose coefficient on each subset is the corresponding value of $z$ when that
subset has size at most $d$, and is zero otherwise. Its value at $x$ equals the sum,
over all subsets of size at most $d$, of the corresponding integer coefficient (viewed
as real) times the sign monomial on that subset.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integer linear threshold representation]
\lean{FABL.exists_integer_linearThresholdRepresentation}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p134-b003}
\label{FABL.exists_integer_linearThresholdRepresentation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsLinearThreshold, FABL.exists_integer_coefficients_of_strict_representation, FABL.exists_positive_strict_shift, FABL.representation_and_ne_zero_of_strict, FABL.signValue, FABL.thresholdSign}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube
$\{-1,1\}^n$ to $\{\pm1\}$. If $f$ is represented as the sign of a real affine
linear form, then there are integer coefficients $a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_n$ such that, for
every $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, $f(x)$ is the sign of $a_0+\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i$, and this
integer-coefficient affine form is nonzero at every point of the cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Integer Fourier coefficients for polynomial thresholds]
\lean{FABL.exists_integer_polynomialThresholdRepresentation}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p134-b003}
\label{FABL.exists_integer_polynomialThresholdRepresentation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsPolynomialThreshold, FABL.IsPolynomialThresholdRepresentation, FABL.exists_integer_coefficients_of_strict_representation, FABL.exists_positive_strict_shift, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierDegree, FABL.fourierDegree_le_iff, FABL.fourier_expansion_unique, FABL.lowDegreeFourierFamily, FABL.monomial, FABL.multilinearPolynomial, FABL.multilinearPolynomial_eq_sum_lowDegree, FABL.representation_and_ne_zero_of_strict, FABL.signValue, FABL.sum_lowDegree_fourierCoeff_eq}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ and $d$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a
Boolean function that has a polynomial threshold representation of Fourier degree at
most $d$. Then there is a real-valued function $p$ on the cube such that $f(x)$ is the
sign of $p(x)$ for every $x$, the Fourier degree of $p$ is at most $d$, every Fourier
coefficient of $p$ is an integer, and $p(x)\ne 0$ for every $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}
